reason: Borates with no transition-metal or lanthanide d/f states have valence bands of O 2p and conduction bands of high-lying cation s states, giving deep-UV transparency; every competing option contains metallic intermetallics, partially filled d/f states (TmMnO3, Li3V12O29, MnCdO2) or heavy-metal narrow-gap chemistry that caps the gap near or below 3 eV.

hypothesis: Ca2Sn2F3, a fluoride with electropositive Ca and Sn(II), should have the widest gap in this menu (roughly 3-4 eV), exceeding the sulfide/selenide semiconductors.
reason: Fluorine's very low-lying 2p valence band produces the largest anion-driven gaps; the remaining options are metallic intermetallics (YNi4B, GaFe3, DySnRu2, TbCu5, Si2Ru, Ho(SiRu)2, Tb(MnGe)6, ZrSiTe semimetal) or chalcogenides whose gaps top out around 2-3.4 eV. hypothesis: CeAlO3, a perovskite oxide of a trivalent rare earth with closed-shell Al, should show the largest gap here (~3 eV or more), well above the heavy chalcogenides and intermetallics.
reason: Oxide perovskites of the LaAlO3 family have O 2p to cation s/d gaps of several eV; substituting Ce lowers it via 4f states but should still exceed the ~1-2.5 eV gaps of InBi2S4Cl, YbTlSe2, Li0.5GePb1.75S4, DyS2 and the metallic/semimetallic borides, carbides and silicide-intermetallics (Pm2PtAu, Y(CrSi)2, CeSiIr, DyNiSn, Dy3MnB7, HoC2).

hypothesis: Zn2Sb3O8 (zinc antimonate) should exhibit the largest experimental gap of this menu, roughly 3-3.7 eV, characteristic of d10 Zn/Sb(V) oxides.
reason: Closed-shell d10 cations with O 2p valence bands give wide-gap transparent oxide semiconductors, unlike the vanadate Na2V6O13 (mixed-valence, near-metallic), metallic LaB6/AlCu3/Ti2MnFe/SmNiC2, and the chalcogenides (Ba2GaSe4, Ba2GaBiS5, GaAgTe2, Ba3SnBiSe8) whose Se/Te-derived valence bands limit gaps to ~1-3 eV; AgP15 is also only ~1.5-2 eV.

hypothesis: The calcium borogermanate Ca10Ge16(B2O17)3 should have the widest gap here (>4 eV, deep-UV transparent), since it contains only closed-shell Ca2+, Ge4+, B3+ and O2-.
reason: Borate/germanate frameworks with no d or f electrons are classic UV nonlinear-optical materials with gaps above 4-5 eV; the alternatives are intermetallics or metals (HfFe2, Mg2Co, NbCrW, Ga9Rh2, Lu2CdAg, Y(CuSi)2, Rb6O suboxide, Ca(BC)2), narrow-gap chalcogenides (KTbSe4, SrUS2), or a Pb/Se-containing oxide whose lone-pair and Se 4p states raise the valence band and shrink the gap.

hypothesis: Na2CdSnS4, a closed-shell d10 quaternary thiostannate, should show the largest experimental band gap in this menu (~3 eV), above the Sb-halide and 3d-metal oxide options.
reason: Most options are intermetallics or 3d transition-metal oxides expected to be metallic or narrow-gap; among the semiconductors, d10 Cd(II)/Sn(IV) sulfides with electropositive Na counterions are typical wide-gap NLO materials, expected to exceed Rb3Sb2Br9 and the Bi/Cr chalcogenide options.

hypothesis: The Pb-Sb sulfoiodide (SbPb2S2I3) should have the widest gap here (~1.8-2.0 eV), above SnSe2 (~1 eV) and Ag7AsS6.

hypothesis: Sr3Se3ClO8, a closed-shell alkaline-earth oxo-halide, should exhibit the largest gap (>4 eV), exceeding the Zn-Ga-Sn oxide and Rb3Sb2I9.

reason: Fluorine substitution into isolated BO3 borate frameworks lowers the valence band and yields deep-UV transparency; the competing candidates are intermetallics, lanthanide transition-metal oxides, or chalcogenides with much narrower expected gaps.

hypothesis: A closed-shell d0 alkaline-earth titanate (BaTi4O8/BaTi4O9-type) should show the widest experimental optical gap in this menu (~3-3.4 eV), exceeding the intermetallics, narrow-gap chalcogenides and Mn/Cu-containing oxides.

hypothesis: K2Al2B2O7, a deep-UV nonlinear-optical borate, will have the largest gap (>6 eV) of this menu.

hypothesis: K2Cd3S4, a closed-shell d10 alkali-metal thiocadmate, will have the largest gap (~3-3.5 eV), above CdS (2.4 eV) because of reduced dimensionality and electropositive K+ spacers.

Competing entries are narrow-gap (GaSb ~0.7 eV, Sn-Pb-Se ~0.3 eV, LuP ~1.3 eV, EuSe ~1.8 eV), metallic (HfFe2, RbCd13, Er2C3, BaGe2), or open-shell/selenide with smaller gaps (LiCuO2, SrUS2, Li2In2SiSe6 ~2.9 eV).

hypothesis: The closed-shell alkali selenogermanate K(GeSe2)2 will show the largest gap (~2.5-2.8 eV) here, since Ge4+/Se2- frameworks with K+ counterions are wide-gap IR-NLO semiconductors.

hypothesis: HfO2, a binary d0 closed-shell early-transition-metal oxide, will show the largest measured gap in this menu (>5 eV), exceeding every other candidate by more than 2 eV.
reason: All other options are either intermetallics/Zintl-like phases (TlZn2Tc, MnSnRu2, SmAg, U3Ni3Sn4, ZrNiSn) that are metallic or near-zero-gap, narrow-gap chalcogenides (PbSe0.9S0.1 ~0.3 eV, LiAsS2 ~2 eV), or partially filled d/f oxides and halides (EuTiClO3, Li4Ni3BiO8, K3Bi2I9 ~2 eV) whose gaps are limited by mid-gap d/f states. hypothesis: NaSc(SeO3)2 is a UV-transparent d0 selenite with an absorption edge below ~320 nm, i.e. a gap above 3.8 eV, larger than the other oxides and semiconductors here.

hypothesis: CuGaO2 (delafossite) will show the largest optical gap in this menu, ~3.4-3.7 eV direct, versus <3 eV for every other candidate.
reason: Cu+ is d10 closed shell and Ga3+ is s0, so there is no partially filled d manifold; CuGaO2 is an archetypal wide-gap p-type transparent conducting oxide. Everything else is gap-narrowing: heavy narrow-gap chalcogenides (PbSe-SnTe alloy, Sr-Ge-Bi-Se, Sm2(SnSe3)3, Cu-Ge-Pb-S), metallic or near-metallic phases (Tl3Cr, CeAgSn, Hf3Zn3N, YB66), and lone-pair/open-shell oxides (Bi2Te2SO10, VZn2BiO6).

hypothesis: H7Se2NO6, a hydrogen-bonded closed-shell light-element selenite salt, is a colorless insulator with a gap above 4 eV, far above the ~2 eV semiconductors in this menu.

Every alternative has a mechanism forcing a small gap: partially filled d states (MnNbO4, Ba3NaIr2O9, Cr(MoS2)2), narrow-gap III-V/II-VI alloys (InSb0.3As0.7, Cd-doped InAs, Zn/Se-doped GaAs), intermetallics and clathrates (TiFe2Si, Te2Pd3, Sr4Ga8Ge15, CsRbP), or lanthanide 4f sulfides (La5SmS8).

hypothesis: LiGaO2, a wide-gap closed-shell ternary oxide of Li+ and d10 Ga3+, will show the largest experimental band gap (~5 eV) in this menu.
reason: The other options are narrow-gap chalcogenides/tellurides (Bi-Sb-Te, PbSe-based, La3Te4, TeAs, AsSI), metallic intermetallics (ScCdAg2, YbSmRh2), or oxides whose gaps are pinned lower by Bi 6p or Ni 3d states (Bi24BO39, Ni2PO5). LiGaO2 combines electropositive Li, a d10 cation and deep O 2p valence states, giving a UV-transparent gap well above the alternatives.

hypothesis: LiCaO3, containing only closed-shell s-block cations with oxide anions, will exhibit the widest experimental gap (>4 eV) in this menu.
reason: Most candidates are intermetallics (Al2Cu, Lu2MgHg, CeMgAg2, ZrNiGe, NdSnRh) expected to be metallic, or medium/narrow-gap chalcogenides and pnictides (ErTe, Ce(CuSb)2, Dy(CuSe)3, ZnSe-based ~2.7 eV, Li2CdSnS4 ~3 eV). Cr2P3O11 is limited by Cr 3d states. Highly ionic alkali/alkaline-earth oxides typically give the largest optical gaps.
